note: POLICY CHANGE FROM NATHAN, 2026-08-18: NO MORE DIRECT PUSHES TO main EXCEPT A HOTFIX. Work goes through the merge queue. His words: let us not do the direct push anymore unless it is a hotfix. WHY, with the measurement that prompted it. A direct push is invisible to the queue, so it races any chamber run in flight. Commit 88379dfa — a ONE-LINE addition to book/src/frontier/idea-registry.md — was pushed while feat/decision-blocks was in the chamber. That candidate had all six phases GREEN; main moved underneath it; pre-push correctly refused a non-fast-forward and the chamber held. An hour of the serial box, discarded, for a candidate with nothing wrong with it. The asymmetry is the whole argument: the pusher pays nothing and the running candidate pays the hour. WHAT TO DO INSTEAD: branch, make gate-commit, push the branch, make sluice BRANCH=<branch> REF=<full 40-char sha>. Remember the Sluice-Headline trailer — the server-side check refuses a merge without one, and it must sit adjacent to your other trailers with NO BLANK LINE between, because git parses only the message last block. THIS IS NOW CHEAP FOR PROSE, WHICH IS WHY THE POLICY IS REASONABLE RATHER THAN CEREMONIAL. A prose-only candidate — every changed path under docs/, book/src/chronicle/, book/src/frontier/, book/src/open-questions.md or book/src/SUMMARY.md — skips seam-guard, clients and heavy, because none of those can observe a prose change. Measured: a three-file docs merge cost 3561 s under the old ladder, of which 3124 s (88%) went to those three. A registry edit through the queue is now roughly 7 minutes rather than 60. IF YOU DO PUSH A HOTFIX: run make sluice-status FIRST. If a chamber run is in flight you will kill it, and the operator cannot hold a run for a push it cannot see. A SEPARATE BRANCH FOR REGISTRY EDITS WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, with the numbers: 12 of the last 20 merges to main touched idea-registry.md and it took 143 commits in seven days. A dedicated branch would be a SECOND writer to a file every campaign already writes as part of its close, so it would not remove the merge — it would guarantee a conflict at every campaign close, and it recreates the long-lived-second-main divergence the board lane is explicitly named to avoid.
